questions.stem: Which functional group defines an alcohol?

options.explanation: The family is defined by the polar hydroxyl group attached to a saturated carbon.
Carbonyls define aldehydes and ketones, not alcohols.
Carboxyl defines carboxylic acids, a different homologous series.
Halogen carriers are halogenoalkanes, not alcohols.

questions.stem: The general formula of the alcohols is

options.explanation: Hydrogen count grows with 2n+1, not with n.
Each extra carbon adds two hydrogens, plus the one in the hydroxyl, giving H2n+1.
That formula runs one hydrogen short for saturated alcohols.
That is the formula of an ether-like composition, not the alcohol series convention.

questions.stem: An alcohol whose -OH carbon is bonded to two other carbon atoms is classified as

options.explanation: Tertiary alcohols carry three carbon neighbours.

options.text: A diol, since two groups are involved
options.explanation: Diol counts hydroxyl groups per molecule, not carbon neighbours.
Two carbon neighbours around the hydroxyl carbon define the secondary class.
Primary alcohols carry only one carbon neighbour.

questions.stem: Which name follows the alcohol naming convention correctly for a three-carbon chain with the hydroxyl on an end carbon?

options.explanation: The suffix drops the final e of the alkane name, giving propan-1-ol.
Numbering starts from the end nearer the hydroxyl, so locant 3 is wrong for an end carbon.
The systematic convention is the -ol suffix with a locant, not this form.
The alkan-ol pattern with locant 1 places the hydroxyl on the first carbon of the propane chain.

questions.stem: A molecule containing two -OH groups on different carbons is called

options.explanation: Two hydroxyl groups on one molecule make a diol by definition.
Classification by carbon neighbours is separate from counting hydroxyl groups.
Hydrates are water-containing solids, not covalent molecules with two -OH groups.
Peroxides contain an O-O bond, which a diol need not have.

questions.stem: State the general formula of the alcohols.
questions.modelAnswer: The alcohols have the general formula CnH2n+1OH, one hydroxyl group per formula unit.

questions.stem: Name the first four members of the alcohol series.
questions.modelAnswer: Methanol, ethanol, propan-1-ol and butan-1-ol, with one, two, three and four carbons respectively.

questions.stem: Explain why ethanol is classified as a primary alcohol.
questions.modelAnswer: In ethanol the carbon carrying the hydroxyl group is bonded to only one other carbon atom, the methyl carbon, and one carbon neighbour is precisely the definition of a primary alcohol.

questions.stem: Classify butan-2-ol and justify the class from its carbon framework.
questions.modelAnswer: Butan-2-ol is secondary: the hydroxyl sits on carbon 2 of the butane chain, and that carbon is bonded to two other carbon atoms, carbons 1 and 3 of the chain.
